_meta.indication: Treatment of primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) in combination with UDCA in adults who have an inadequate response to UDCA, or as monotherapy in patients unable to tolerate UDCA

pivotal_trials.design: Multi-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study; patients randomized to IQIRVO 80 mg or placebo once daily for at least 52 weeks
pivotal_trials.population: 161 adults with PBC with an inadequate response or intolerance to UDCA
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Biochemical response at Week 52, defined as ALP less than 1.67-times ULN, TB less than or equal to ULN, and ALP decrease greater than or equal to 15% from baseline
pivotal_trials.result: Biochemical response rate 51% (55/108) with IQIRVO vs 4% (2/53) placebo; treatment difference 47% (95% CI 32, 57), p<0.0001. ALP normalization 15% vs 0%, difference 15% (95% CI 6, 23), p=0.0019.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥5% and ≥1% higher than placebo): weight gain 23% vs 21%, diarrhea 11% vs 9%, abdominal pain 11% vs 6%, nausea 11% vs 6%, vomiting 11% vs 2%. Serious risks include myalgia/myopathy/rhabdomyolysis, fractures, and drug-induced liver injury.
target_moa: Elafibranor and its active metabolite GFT1007 are peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor (PPAR) agonists that activate PPAR-alpha, PPAR-gamma, and PPAR-delta; the exact mechanism in PBC is not well understood

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because there were no issues that warranted an advisory committee discussion.
